articles.summary: Sallie Mae ® (Nasdaq: SLM), formally SLM Corporation, today announced Chief Executive Officer Jon Witter will participate in a fireside chat at the TD Cowen 2026 Financials Fintech Conference on Tuesday, Nov. 17, at 11:45 a.m. ET. A live audio webcast and replay will be available at SallieMae.com/investors . Sallie Mae (Nasdaq: SLM) believes education and life-long learning, in all forms, help people achieve great things. As the leader in private student lending, we provide financing and know-how to support access to college and offer products and resources to help customers make new goals and experiences, beyond college, happen. Learn more at SallieMae.com . Commonly known as Sallie Mae, SLM Corporation and its subsidiaries are not sponsored by or agencies of the United States of America. articles.summary: The Bridging the Dream Scholarship Program Provides $10,000 Scholarships to 30 High School Seniors and 20 Graduate Students Nationwide In celebration of National Scholarship Month, Sallie today announced the newest recipients of its Bridging the Dream Scholarship Program. The Sallie Mae Fund, in partnership with the Thurgood Marshall College Fund (TMCF), awarded $500,000 in scholarships to help students access and complete higher education. Through this year’s program, 30 high school seniors received $10,000 scholarships based on financial need, academic achievement, leadership, and service. In addition, 20 graduate students pursuing advanced degrees also received $10,000 scholarships. Since 2021, The Sallie Mae Fund has awarded more than $5.5 million in scholarships to nearly 1,500 students through its Bridging the Dream and Completing the Dream Scholarship Programs . articles.summary: Simple Tips Can Help Students and Families Find More Opportunities and Avoid Missing Out on Free Money for College Nearly 8 in 10 families who used scholarships in the 2025-26 academic year said that money helped make college possible, according to Sallie’s How America Pays for College 2026 . This National Scholarship Month, Sallie is dispelling myths and misconceptions about scholarships to help students and families access free money that can make college affordable. That’s particularly important given nearly half (48%) of families believe scholarships are only reserved for students with exceptional grades or abilities, 41% think they are only available to incoming freshmen, and 35% believe their family’s income is too high to qualify. The reality is scholarships are available for a wide variety of interests and backgrounds, more than half are available for current college students, and not all are based on financial need.
